html:
Portuguese Angola was the Portuguese colony that grew from the founding of Luanda in 1576 into modern Angola, ruled by Portugal for four centuries until independence in 1975.

For most of that time its main business was the slave trade. Wars against Ndongo, whose queen Nzinga fought Portugal for decades, and trade with inland states supplied captives shipped from Luanda and Benguela, mostly to Brazil. Angola was the largest single source of people in the Atlantic slave trade, several million in all.

The coast only was ruled until the late 19th century, when Portugal conquered the interior. In the 20th century white settlers came in large numbers, coffee and diamonds became exports, and forced labour was common, until the war of independence began in 1961.
sum: Portuguese Angola was the Portuguese colony that grew from the founding of Luanda in 1576 into modern Angola, ruled by Portugal for four centuries until independence in 1975.
